name: Musia
subtitle: Hear the beat. Play along.
short_description: Practice guitar at your pace with song loops, chord shapes and a steady pulse.
description:
Know a few guitar chords, but lose your place when the song starts? Musia connects listening, sung phrases and chord changes in one native practice workspace. You do not need to sing before you begin.

HEAR ONE SMALL STEP
Play Do, Re and Mi reference tones, then try a listening quiz. Expand to a full octave when ready. The score counts your first answer, not your singing or guitar performance. These sounds work offline.

FIND A STEADY PULSE
Begin with First Pulse, a synthesized Em/Am reference exercise. Or choose 40-160 BPM in the metronome, hear the accented first beat and add an Em/Am change every four beats. Start with one comfortable down-strum on beat one.

RETURN TO THE SAME PHRASE
Slow a song from 25% to 200% speed while preserving pitch. Loop one lyric phrase or set A/B markers. Follow the current and next chord with finger positions, open/muted strings and barre markings. All 24 major/minor chord shapes are included.

FOLLOW WORDS AND MUSIC TOGETHER
Explore creator-made recordings with English, Chinese and Japanese performances. Show several lyric languages together, with pinyin and furigana where available. Translations follow the selected recording; changing the displayed languages does not change the voice. Keep listening with background playback and native media controls. Catalog streaming requires an internet connection.

KEEP PRACTICE LOCAL
Find your sessions in Settings > Practice history. Export or clear them when you choose. No account, advertising or subscription is required.

Song chords, beats and melody obtained through automatic analysis remain estimates, not a verified score. Tap feedback includes device/audio latency. Musia does not record your microphone, grade instruments, analyze user uploads or provide in-app AI song generation.
review_notes:
0.1.2 (4) adds substantive beginner practice and multilingual playback features beyond rejected 0.1.1. Our response to all nine 4.3/4.2.6 questions, with native screenshots and shared-code disclosures, is attached in App Review correspondence. This is our own song-based practice product and creator-curated content, not a client app or commercial template.

No login, subscription, microphone permission or special hardware is required.
1. Library > First Pulse: four count-in beats; Em/Am changes at 4, 8, 12 and 16 seconds. Try Listen/Tap/Play, slower speed and a phrase loop. This known reference works offline.
2. Library > Aya Chan / Rain of Light: play a vocal, select EN/ZH/JA lyrics independently, and follow pronunciation readings and analyzed chords. Catalog songs need internet.
3. Lessons > Do Re Mi: play reference tones, then Quiz. The first answer scores; there is no microphone or singing grade.
4. Lessons > Metronome: choose 60 BPM, start and enable Em/Am chord practice. Chords change every four beats from the audio playhead. Leave the exercise to stop clicks. Normal song background playback is separate.
5. Settings > Practice history: inspect, export or clear local sessions.

Analyzed song data is labeled as estimates; tap feedback includes output latency. The app does not expose desktop AI-generation tools. Our small founder-led TestFlight feedback and engineering test limits are described separately in the response; no large user study is claimed. The owner confirmed commercial distribution rights for recordings, lyrics, translations and artwork.
release_notes: Beginner Do Re Mi listening practice, adjustable metronome with Em/Am changes, simultaneous English/Chinese/Japanese lyrics with available pinyin/furigana, and Practice history under Settings.
